issue.title: Prompt-history xprompt chips include #hex colors from directive arguments (e.g. %clan summary markup)
issue.description:
Prompt-history xprompt chips (the TAGS column in the prompt history modal, and any other
consumer of `summarize_prompt_for_list` / `summarize_prompt_for_preview`) report false
xprompt chips for `#`-prefixed text inside directive arguments. A real launch prompt whose
preamble contains `%clan(toobig-5x, tribe=chop, summary=[[[bold #D75FFF]◆ TOOBIG SPLIT · 5 FILES[/bold #D75FFF]…)`
yields `xprompts == ('#D75FFF', '#D7D7FF', '#A8A8A8')`: Rich color markup in the clan summary
argument is treated as three xprompt references.

Root cause: `_scan_prompt_controls` in `src/sase/history/prompt_metadata.py` scans directives
and `iter_xprompt_references` over the same protected text independently, and
`_embedded_xprompt_chips` / `_embedded_xprompt_refs` never exclude references whose span lies
inside a directive token's span (the directive intervals are already available on
`_PromptControlScan.directives`). The fix is to drop refs contained in any directive
interval before building chips/refs (and add a regression test with a `%clan(..., summary=[bold #D75FFF]...)` prompt).

Found while designing the agent-tribe PROMPTS section (plan tribe_panel_prompts), which
sidesteps this by computing chips from the preamble-stripped body; prompt history does not.

task_type_fields.impact: Prompt history TAGS column (and any summarize_prompt_for_list consumer) shows bogus green xprompt chips like #D75FFF for launch prompts whose directives carry Rich markup, crowding out real xprompt chips in a 16-cell column.
task_type_fields.repro:
.venv/bin/python -c "from sase.history.prompt_metadata import summarize_prompt_for_list as s; print(s('%clan(toobig-5x, tribe=chop, summary=[bold #D75FFF]x[/bold #D75FFF])\n%id:a.0\nCan you split foo.py?').xprompts)"
Expected: () — Observed: ('#D75FFF', ...) hex colors from the directive argument. Reproduced on real artifact ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/artifacts/ace-run/202609/23/20260923071627/raw_xprompt.md, which yields ('#D75FFF', '#D7D7FF', '#A8A8A8').
